column1: So recall that if I have a proper ideal in a ring, then we call the thing maximal if and only if any ideal stuck between the this ideal and the entire ring must be either that ideal or the entire ring, so there's nothing sort of properly stuck between.

column1: Now what was our sort of clever way of characterizing maximal ideals in terms of quotients of a ring? Fields, exactly! So here's the theorem: M is a maximal ideal if and only if R mod M is a field.
column2: 那么我们之前用商环刻画极大理想的巧妙方法是什么？域，完全正确！定理如下：M 是极大理想当且仅当 R/M 是一个域。

column1: And this is because we understand this structure of the ideals of a quotient: if we knew the lattice of ideals in a particular ring, then we could figure out the lattice of ideals in any quotient of it; and we know that fields are characterized by they're having these two ideals: the zero ideal and the full ideal, the unit ideal, and them being distinct.
column2: 这是因为我们了解商环的理想结构：如果我们知道某个环中的理想格，我们就能求出其任意商环中的理想格；而我们知道域的特征是恰好有两个不同的理想：零理想与全理想（单位理想）。

column2: 主要原因在于：说 p 整除某元素，等价于说该元素落在由它生成的理想中，所以定义显然是等价的。

column1: In other words, p divides a implies p divides a or p divides b can be translated under this into just saying that ab is in this ideal generated by p implies a is in the ideal generated by p or b is in the ideal generated by p. Is that clear? Any questions about this?
column2: 换句话说，p | ab 蕴含 p | a 或 p | b 在此对应下可直接翻译为：ab 属于这个由 p 生成的理想，蕴含 a 属于由 p 生成的理想，或 b 属于由 p 生成的理想。清楚了吗？对此有什么疑问吗？

column1: Okay. Now do I have any reason to think that if I have a prime ideal in general, then it must be generated as the principal ideal by some prime element?

column1: Absolutely not! In fact, it's absolutely false that in general a prime ideal is going to be generated by some prime element, so don't make this mistake; so these are distinct ideas.
column2: 绝非如此！事实上，素理想一般由某个素元生成是彻底错误的，所以不要犯这个错误；这是截然不同的概念。

column1: So this is sort of a statement, of course, analogous to the proposition we had over here that maximal is characterized by the quotient being a field.
column2: 这当然与我们这边的命题类似，即极大理想由商环为域来刻画。

column1: And this is pretty obvious; does anybody want to go through the proof of this? Okay, sure, so I'll go through a proof of this.

column2: 现在根据假设，由于 P 是素理想，这蕴含 x̃ ∈ P 或ỹ ∈ P，但这正是说 x = 0 或 y = 0，同样是由于商环的定义。这清楚了吗？

column1: So this is a very easy result, it's a very nice characterization; and one of the best ways of thinking in general about domains is, sorry, about prime ideals is that they have quotients being domains. Now what's a sort of immediate corollary of this? We know that every field is a domain, right?
column2: 所以这是非常容易的结论，是一个极好的刻画；并且在一般情况下思考素理想的最佳方式之一，就是它们的商环是整环。那么这的一个直接推论是什么？我们知道每个域都是整环，对吧？

column1: Because we can take these, because we can, you know, if we had some xy equal to zero in a field, then we could always just multiply by an inverse unless, you know, one of the things is zero.
column2: 因为……如果我们有域中的某个 xy = 0，那么只要其中一个因子不为零，我们总能乘以逆元。

column1: So what does that tell us about the relationship between maximal and prime ideals?
column2: 所以这告诉了我们极大理想与素理想之间的什么关系？

column2: 极……完全正确，所以一个直接推论是：如果 M是极大理想，则 M 是素理想；证明当然就是 R/M 为域蕴含 R/M 是整环。

So this is another nice sort of characterization of the relationship between domains and things like primes.
column2: 所以 R 是整环……当且仅当 (0) 是素理想；证明在于 R ≅ R/(0)，所以该环是整环，换言之 R 是整环当且仅当零理想是素理想。所以这是整环与素理想之间关系的又一个优美刻画。

column1: Okay, excellent!

column1: So we've talked about a sort of string of special ideals, and they had this nice sort of filtered form: we had these, you know, most general things, all rings, and then descending all the way down to fields.

column1: Now I want to talk about something which doesn't quite fit into that filtration; it's sort of something parallel to that filtration, and it's not described explicitly in Artin, which is a pity, because a lot of what's going on in Artin in Sections 11.10 and thereabouts are really sort of... they seem like these weird sort of disjointed results which have nothing to do with ring theory in general.
column2: 现在我想讨论一些并不完全契合该层级的内容；它与该层级平行，并且在阿廷的书中没有明确阐述，这很遗憾，因为阿廷书中第 11.10 节及附近的内容，真的……看起来像是离散古怪的结论，与一般的环论毫无关系。

column1: So I'm going to, in an extremely simplified form, explain the underlying theory behind what's happening there; and I think that this is useful, because I think otherwise it's very difficult to remember what's going on—it just seems like a bunch of like random things about quadratic fields.
column2: 因此我要以极度简化的形式，解释背后发生的基础理论；我认为这很有用，因为否则很难记住究竟是怎么回事——它看起来就像一堆关于二次域的零碎性质。

column1: But these are not random things about quadratic fields; they're actually very general and deep and important results, and they are about these things called Dedekind domains.
column2: 但这些绝非关于二次域的随机琐事，它们实际上是非常一般、深刻且重要的定理，它们是关于被称为戴德金整环（Dedekind domains）的对象。

column1: Now there are very complicated definitions of Dedekind domains, but there's also an extremely simple definition of Dedekind domain which is usually omitted from most textbooks,
column2: 戴德金整环有非常复杂的定义，但也有一个极其简单的定义，通常大多数教科书都忽略了它，这是有充分理由的，

column1: and for a very good reason, because by the time you usually get data domains you've built up a whole bunch of extra theory, but you don't need it: the only piece of theory that I need to introduce is the notion of multiplication of ideals.
column2: 因为通常当你学到戴德金整环时，已经建立了一大堆额外的理论；但其实你不需要那些：我唯一需要引入的理论，就是理想的乘法概念。

column1: So if I have some ideals I and J in R, then I define their product to be... what?
column2: 如果我在 R 中有理想 I 和 J，那么我把它们的乘积定义为……什么？

column1: Can anybody tell me what the product of two ideals is?
column2: 有人能告诉我两个理想的乘积是什么吗？

column1: Exactly, is the set of all finite sums of a_i b_i, where the a_i are in I and the b_i are in J.
column2: 完全正确，它是所有有限和 ∑ a_i b_i 的集合，其中 a_i ∈ I 且 b_i ∈ J。

column1: You need the find sums, of course, because you need this thing to be an ideal: you want to define the product of ideals to be some ideal.
column2: 你当然需要有限和，因为你需要它是一个理想：你希望将理想的乘积定义为一个理想。

column1: If you just had products, then you wouldn't necessarily know that for something which is not for instance generated by a single element—for if I or J were not principal—you would not know that the thing would be closed under addition. So you need to have these finite sums to make sure that the things are actually a subgroup.
column2: 如果你只取乘积元素，你未必知道对于非单元素生成的理想——如果 I 或 J 不是主理想——该集合对加法是否封闭。所以你需要这些有限和来确保它确实是一个子群。

column1: And it's very easy to verify this is an ideal: I mean it's certainly a subgroup because you have these sums and so on, and it's closed under multiplication by R by the fact that I and J were individually so.
column2: 而且很容易验证这是一个理想：它当然是一个加法子群，因为有这些和式等等，并且由 I 和 J 各自的性质可知它在 R 的乘法下封闭。

column1: Now just to make sure that we're all on the same page: if I do have two principal ideals, say (a) and (b), so this is I and this is J, then what is the product IJ?

column1: So in this extremely simple case, what is the multiple of the ideal generated by a and the ideal generated by b? Exactly, the ideal generated by ab.
column2: 在这种极其简单的情形下，由 a 生成的理想与由 b 生成的理想的乘积是什么？正是由 ab 生成的主理想 (ab)。

column1: So at least when you have principal ideals, this is the simplest possible operation, it's just multiplication of elements. Is that pretty clear?
column2: 所以至少在处理主理想时，这是最简单的运算，就只是元素的乘法。这很清楚了吗？

column1: Are there any questions about this? Okay, good. So as I promised, here's another type of special ring.

column1: Then we say R is a Dedekind domain if for every ideal, there's a sort of other ideal which when you multiply by this ideal gives you a principal ideal.
column2: 那么我们称 R 为戴德金整环，如果对每个理想，都存在另一个理想，与该理想相乘后得到一个主理想。

column1: All the results there you can prove without working in a quadratic field, but just with the sort of assumption that I'm going to write down. So for all ideals, there exists another ideal such that their product is principal.
column2: 那里的所有结论，你无需局限在二次域中即可证明，只需利用我即将写下的假设。所以：对所有理想，都存在另一个理想使得它们的乘积为主理想。

column1: So I multiply these things, and this thing is principal; and I'm going to assume of course that this J is not equal to the zero ideal, otherwise I'd have this trivially true.

column1: So if there's some nonzero ideal such that this thing is principal... So here's an example which is worked out in the book, and I highly recommend that you work out why it's true, because it gives you an idea of what happens in greater generality.

column1: So suppose I start out with Q join root D, where d is square-free, some square-free integer. So I'm going to use a slightly different notation, because it's actually the general notation used in the literature: in the book, the letter R is used for the ring of integers in a quadratic field; in general the notation is O_K.
column2: 假设我们从 Q(√d) 出发，其中 d 是无平方因子的，某个无平方因子的整数。我要使用一种略有不同的记号，因为这其实是文献中的通用记号：在书中，字母 R 用于表示二次域中的整数环；一般记号是 O_K。

column1: The reason for the O is that there's this terminology of order—I'm not going to explain this right now, but the idea is that O_K is this sort of something called the maximal order in K; but suffice it to say that that's a synonym for the ring of all algebraic integers in K. column2: 用 O 的原因在于有"整序"这个术语——我不会在此详述，但其含义是 O_K 是 K 中的所谓"极大整序"；只需记住它是K 中所有代数整数构成的环的同义词。我们知道它的结构，那么它是什么？

column1: Remember, to prove something is a Dedekind domain, you need to show that for every ideal, you can multiply by some other ideal, and that product had better be principal; that's what you need to show.
